title: AgentScript-Eval: Benchmarking LLMs and Agents for Code Generation in an Enterprise DSL
abstract: arXiv:2611.13183v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Domain-specific languages (DSLs) are widely used in enterprise software, giving a compact interface to complex tasks, from data access to infrastructure automation. Platforms increasingly extend them to agents, where a developer declares the topics, permitted actions, and guardrails of an agent rather than writing general-purpose code. Large language models (LLMs) write general-purpose code well, but that ability has been measured almost entirely on languages abundant in public pretraining data, and enterprise DSLs are neither abundant nor public. We introduce AgentScript-Eval, an execution-graded benchmark of 100 real tasks for AgentScript, the declarative DSL that Salesforce uses in Agentforce to build conversational agents. Tasks span authoring an agent from a specification, debugging a broken definition, and optimizing a working one. Evaluating five models zero-shot, we find that the regime is hard: the best model reaches only 25.0

translated_title: AgentScript-Eval：在企业级领域专用语言（DSL）中评估LLM与智能体代码生成能力的基准测试
translated_abstract: 领域专用语言（DSL）在企业软件中被广泛使用，为从数据访问到基础设施自动化等复杂任务提供了紧凑的接口。平台正日益将DSL扩展至智能体场景，开发者通过声明智能体的主题、允许的操作和防护机制来构建智能体，而非编写通用代码。大型语言模型（LLM）擅长编写通用代码，但这种能力几乎完全是在公开预训练数据中广泛存在的语言上测量的，而企业级DSL既不常见也不公开。我们提出了AgentScript-Eval，这是一个基于执行结果评分的基准，包含100个针对AgentScript的真实任务。AgentScript是Salesforce在Agentforce中用于构建对话式智能体的声明式DSL。任务涵盖根据规范编写智能体、调试损坏的定义以及优化可正常工作的定义。通过对五个模型进行零样本评估，我们发现这一领域极具挑战性：表现最好的模型仅达到25.0（原文截断，应为25.0%）的通过率。
tldr: 该论文提出了AgentScript-Eval基准，包含100个针对Salesforce企业级声明式DSL（AgentScript）的真实任务，首次系统评估了LLM和智能体在企业DSL上的代码生成能力，发现该任务极具挑战性，最佳模型零样本通过率仅为25.0%。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces AgentScript-Eval, an execution-graded benchmark of 100 real tasks for Salesforce's enterprise declarative DSL AgentScript, providing the first systematic evaluation of LLMs and agents on code generation in enterprise DSLs, revealing that the task is highly challenging with the best model achieving only 25.0% in zero-shot evaluation.
